stem: In triangle \(ABC\), \(\overline{BI}\) bisects angle \(ABC\), and \(\overline{CI}\) bisects angle \(ACB\). The measure of angle \(BAC\) is \(52^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(BIC\)?
solution: The other two angles of triangle \(ABC\) add up to \(180 - 52 = 128^{\circ}\). Neither one is needed separately.
The bisectors take half of each: angle \(IBC\) + angle \(ICB = \frac{128}{2} = 64^{\circ}\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-52)<0.1
assert abs(ang('A','B','I')-ang('I','B','C'))<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','I')-ang('I','C','B'))<0.1
ans=180-Rational(180-52,2)
assert abs(ang('B','I','C')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==116
